Not applicable - given by deep IM injection, not oral

summary: Hydroxyprogesterone caproate is a long-acting synthetic progestin given by deep intramuscular injection in an oil vehicle. The older labeled (non-pregnant) uses are advanced endometrial adenocarcinoma, amenorrhea, abnormal uterine bleeding due to hormonal imbalance, and as a test for endogenous estrogen. As Makena, a 250 mg weekly IM dose was once used to reduce recurrent preterm birth, but the FDA withdrew that approval in 2023 after confirmatory trials failed to show benefit. It is contraindicated in thromboembolic disease, hormone-sensitive cancers, and liver disease.
indications: Reduction of risk of recurrent preterm birth in women with a singleton pregnancy and a prior spontaneous preterm birth (former Makena indication - FDA approval withdrawn April 2023)
Advanced adenocarcinoma of the uterine corpus (Stage III or IV) in non-pregnant women
Abnormal uterine bleeding due to hormonal imbalance in the absence of organic pathology
Test for endogenous estrogen production and production of secretory endometrium and desquamation (Medical D and C)

dosage.c: Reduction of recurrent preterm birth (former Makena use)
dosage.t: Begin between 16 0/7 and 20 6/7 weeks; continue until 37 weeks or delivery
dosage.n: FDA withdrew this indication in April 2023; confirmatory PROLONG trial did not show benefit

dosage.d: 1,000 mg or more, 1 or more times weekly (1 to 7 g/week)
dosage.t: Start at once; reassess by 12 weeks
dosage.n: Stop on relapse or after 12 weeks with no objective response; not for early-stage disease

dosage.d: 375 mg, then per cyclic therapy schedule (often with estradiol valerate every 4 weeks)
dosage.t: Any time; repeat every 4 weeks; stop after 4 cycles
dosage.n: Exclude genital malignancy first; acts as a Medical D and C

dosage.t: Any time; confirm with 2nd injection 4 weeks later
dosage.n: Bleeding 7-14 days after injection indicates endogenous estrogen

admin: Intramuscular use ONLY - inject deeply into the upper outer quadrant of the gluteal muscle
A small-gauge needle may be used because of the low viscosity of the oil vehicle; administer the full dose as the 250 mg/mL concentration is in a small volume
Inspect visually for particulate matter and discoloration before use; solution is a clear pale-yellow to yellow oil
A wet needle or syringe may cause cloudiness, which does not affect potency
Protect from light; store vial in its box, upright; discard any unused product within 5 weeks after first use
Crystals may form at low storage temperatures and redissolve on warming in boiling water
moa: Hydroxyprogesterone is a potent, long-acting progestational steroid ester that binds progesterone receptors, transforming a proliferative (estrogen-primed) endometrium into a secretory endometrium, inducing mammary duct development, and inhibiting the production/release of gonadotropins. It has only slight estrogenic, androgenic, or corticoid activity. The proposed (now unproven for efficacy) basis for preterm-birth prevention is progesterone's myometrial quiescence and maintenance of pregnancy.

absolute: Known or suspected breast carcinoma or other hormone-sensitive cancer (or history)
Current or history of thrombotic or thromboembolic disorders (DVT, PE, MI, stroke)
Use as a diagnostic test for pregnancy
Known hypersensitivity to the drug or a progestin
relative: Conditions worsened by fluid retention - asthma, migraine, epilepsy, cardiac or renal dysfunction
monitor: Signs of thromboembolism and neuro-ocular events

preg: Was administered during pregnancy as Makena (250 mg IM weekly) to reduce recurrent preterm birth, but the FDA formally withdrew this approval in April 2023 after confirmatory data failed to demonstrate efficacy. The other labeled hormonal uses are for NON-pregnant women, and the drug is contraindicated as a pregnancy test and in missed abortion. Do not use for preterm-birth prevention outside of any remaining specialist/guideline context.
lact: Detectable amounts of progestins appear in the milk of mothers receiving the drug. Many studies have found no adverse effect of progestins on breastfeeding performance or on infant health, growth, or development; generally considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: The effect of renal impairment on the pharmacokinetics of hydroxyprogesterone caproate has not been evaluated. Use with caution; fluid retention may worsen renal dysfunction.
hepatic: Contraindicated in liver dysfunction or disease. Hydroxyprogesterone caproate is extensively hepatically metabolized (predominantly CYP3A4/3A5), and hepatic impairment may reduce its elimination; the effect of impairment on PK has not been formally studied.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) may lower progestin exposure and efficacy
moderate: Strong CYP3A4/3A5 inhibitors (ketoconazole, ritonavir, clarithromycin) may increase exposure
Antidiabetic agents - progestins may decrease glucose tolerance and raise requirements
minor: Estrogens used concomitantly in cyclic regimens (combined hormonal considerations)
interactions.food: Not applicable - administered intramuscularly, not affected by food
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction with the injection; alcohol is not relevant to dosing
interactions.diagnostics: May alter laboratory tests: increased sulfobromophthalein (hepatic) retention, increased prothrombin and clotting Factors VII/VIII/IX/X, increased PBI and butanol-extractable protein-bound iodine, and decreased T3 uptake (thyroid tests)

common: Injection-site pain, soreness, swelling, itching, bruising
Breakthrough bleeding, spotting, or withdrawal bleeding
serious: Arterial/venous thromboembolism - DVT, PE (some fatal), MI, stroke
Decreased glucose tolerance / hyperglycemia in diabetics
rare: Allergic rash, hirsutism, scalp hair loss
Coughing, dyspnea, chest constriction, allergic-like reactions (more likely at higher doses)
emergency: Signs of clot: leg swelling/pain, chest pain, breathlessness, sudden severe headache, sudden vision loss/diplopia/proptosis
Severe allergic / anaphylactoid reaction with dyspnea or chest constriction

monitoring: Signs and symptoms of thromboembolic and neuro-ocular events (vision change, diplopia, proptosis, migraine) - discontinue and examine if they occur
Mood and depression (discontinue if serious depression recurs)
Pretreatment and periodic breast and pelvic examination with Papanicolaou smear
counsel: This medicine is given as a deep injection into the muscle by a healthcare professional
Injection-site pain, soreness, swelling, itching, or bruising is common; report increasing discomfort, oozing of blood/fluid, or inflammation at the site
Seek urgent care for leg swelling/pain, chest pain, breathlessness, sudden severe headache, or sudden vision changes
Tell your clinician if you have diabetes, depression, asthma, migraine, epilepsy, or heart/kidney problems
The preterm-birth (Makena) use was withdrawn by the FDA in 2023 - discuss alternatives with your obstetrician
Report any unusual or abnormal vaginal bleeding
pk: Long-acting depot; gradual release from the IM oil vehicle
Serum peak ~3-7 days after a single IM dose (studied at 1,000 mg in non-pregnant women)
Long, sustained release supporting weekly dosing; pharmacokinetics of the 250 mg dose not formally studied
Prolonged - supports weekly (preterm-birth) or every-4-week (cyclic) dosing
20-25°C (68-77°F); protect from light; store vial in box, upright; discard unused product within 5 weeks of first use
pearls: FDA withdrew the Makena (hydroxyprogesterone caproate) approval for preterm-birth prevention in April 2023 after the confirmatory PROLONG trial failed to confirm benefit
It is for intramuscular use ONLY - never give intravenously; inject deep into the upper outer gluteal quadrant
Contraindicated in any current or prior thromboembolic disease and in hormone-sensitive cancers
Metabolized predominantly by CYP3A4/3A5, so strong inducers/inhibitors can alter exposure
Discard the multidose vial within 5 weeks of first use and protect from light; crystals from cold storage redissolve on warming
Progestins can reduce glucose tolerance - monitor blood glucose in diabetic patients
missed: For the weekly (preterm-birth) regimen, a missed dose should be given as soon as possible; for the every-4-week cyclic regimens follow the schedule and resume as directed by the clinician. Because injections are administered by a healthcare provider, do not attempt to make up doses without medical advice.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Excess progestin exposure may cause nausea, headache, breast tenderness, fluid retention, and breakthrough bleeding, with higher doses increasing the likelihood of allergic-like reactions (cough, dyspnea, chest constriction) and thromboembolic risk. Manage supportively and symptomatically with monitoring.
